successCriteria.description: In `create()`, before calling `mapRow(result.rows[0])`, add a guard that checks `result.rows.length > 0`. If zero rows returned, throw a descriptive error (e.g., `new Error('INSERT did not return a row')`).

In `update()`, before calling `mapRow(result.rows[0])`, add a guard that checks `result.rows.length > 0`. If zero rows returned, throw a `NotFoundError` (imported from `src/shared/errors/index.ts`) with a message indicating the employee was not found.
Replace `throw new Error('No fields to update')` at line 142 with `throw new ValidationError('No fields to update')`, importing `ValidationError` from `src/shared/errors/index.ts`.

Existing unit tests in `tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.test.ts` continue to pass after the changes, and new test cases are added to cover: (a) `create()` when INSERT returns zero rows, (b) `update()` when no fields are provided (ValidationError), (c) `update()` when the employee ID does not exist (NotFoundError).

constraints: Must import `ValidationError` and `NotFoundError` from `src/shared/errors/index.ts` — do not create new error classes or inline error definitions.
Must follow GP-006: all async errors must be caught and handled — the guards must throw synchronously after `await pool.query()` so the promise rejection path is explicit.
Only modify `src/modules/employee/employee.repository.ts` and its corresponding test file `tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.test.ts`.
outOfScope: Changes to any repository other than `employee.repository.ts` (e.g., `leave.repository.ts`, `policy.repository.ts`, `balance.repository.ts`).
Changes to service-layer error handling, controller error mapping, or route-level try/catch blocks.
Adding guards to `findById`, `findByEmployeeNumber`, `findByEmail`, or any read methods — these already safely handle zero rows by returning `null`.
Adding guards to the `delete` method — the intent only addresses `create` and `update`.

ambiguities.description: The intent specifies what error to throw for the `update()` zero-row guard (`NotFoundError`) but does not specify what error to throw for the `create()` zero-row guard. Should `create()` throw a generic `Error`, a `ValidationError`, or a different error type?
options: Throw a generic Error with a descriptive message (e.g., 'INSERT did not return a row')
Throw a ValidationError since the input may have been invalid
Throw a new InternalError or similar 500-level error since this indicates a database-level failure
